subject: Order form & term adjustment — CobaltHealth renewal paperwork
messages:
From: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@cobalthealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@cobalthealth.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Order form & term adjustment — draft redlines

Stephanie — thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our suggested redline to the order form (CobaltHealth_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). High level: we are asking to move the renewal term to 24 months from 36, and to add the +30% capacity uplift for year 1 (to support Q1 pilots). Pricing is in the redline.

Two specific asks from procurement/legal:
- Add a termination-for-convenience right on our side with 30 days notice and pro-rated refund for unused committed capacity.
- Include a data residency commitment (US-only) and confirmation of SOC 2 Type II availability.

We need to get legal sign-off and a PO in place by Dec 10 to hit our internal procurement window. Can you confirm Redwood can accept a 24-month term (or provide an alternative) and confirm SOC2 availability?

Attachments: CobaltHealth_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx

Thanks,
Elaine Porter
Head of Procurement | CobaltHealth

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-12-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form & term adjustment — draft redlines

Hi Elaine — thanks for the redline and for laying out the timeline. Looping in Marcus (AE) and Laura (Legal) and Vanessa (CS) to weigh in. Quick responses to your asks:

- Term: We can be flexible on term length; two options to consider: (A) 24-month term as requested with a slightly higher unit price in year 1, or (B) keep 36 months and apply a one-time pro-rated capacity uplift for the first 12 months. Marcus, can you pull pricing delta for (A) vs (B)?
- Termination for convenience: Laura — can legal propose language that protects Redwood while giving procurement comfort?
- SOC 2 & data residency: Vanessa — CobaltHealth asked for SOC 2 Type II and US-only residency. Vanessa, please confirm what we can provide and estimated delivery of artifacts.

Next steps: Laura to provide a redline for the MSA/order form. Marcus to confirm pricing impact. If we can agree on the T&C this week, I will produce an execution-ready order form and send via DocuSign.

I attached a short summary of the customer redlines I pulled (Redline_Summary.pdf) to make review easier.

Can everyone aim to have legal comments back by EOD Thursday so we can hit Elaine’s Dec 10 sign-off?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@cobalthealth.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-02T09:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form & term adjustment — draft redlines

Stephanie / team — I reviewed Elaine’s draft. High-level legal position and proposed language attached (Draft_MSA_Amendment_redline.docx). Key points:

1) Termination for convenience: we can accept a customer termination-for-convenience, but need the following protections: 60-day notice (commercially reasonable window), pro-rated refund of pre-paid committed capacity only (no retroactive credits for consumed usage), and a mutual termination-for-material-breach carveout. Proposed clause in doc.

2) Liability and cap: we should not change the liability cap or indemnities in the MSA. Any carveouts need to be narrowly scoped.

3) Data residency / SOC 2: we confirm SOC 2 Type II and can provide the report under NDA; we will not change the residency guarantee in the MSA but can add a commitment to host customer data in US regions and to share a subprocessor list. Vanessa, we should confirm the exact timeline for producing the SOC report and the subprocessor list to Elaine.

I added inline comments on the order form pricing table (see doc). If procurement insists on 30-day notice, we can counter with a 45-day compromise.

Will await Marcus on pricing sensitivity for 24 vs 36 months.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Lead Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Elaine Porter <elaine.porter@cobalthealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@cobalthealth.com>, procurement@cobalthealth.com
Date: 2027-12-02T14:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form & term adjustment — draft redlines

Laura — appreciate the quick review and the suggested language. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Notice period: Procurement will accept 45 days notice for termination-for-convenience (team prefers 45 over 60).
- Refund mechanics: we agree one-time pro-rated refund for unused committed capacity is acceptable; need the exact calculation formula in the order form (days remaining / days in term * unused committed units).
- SOC 2 / subprocessor list: we require that the SOC 2 Type II report be provided to our security team prior to signature and that a current subprocessor list be included.

Timeline: we have an internal approval meeting on Dec 9; if we have an execution-ready order form and a PO by EOD Dec 10 we can process payment during the week of Dec 13. I attached a PO stub for reference (PO_CobaltHealth_Dec2027.pdf).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want to finalize language.

Elaine Porter
Head of Procurement | CobaltHealth

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Order form & term adjustment — CobaltHealth renewal paperwork (next steps)

Elaine — thanks, all. Quick summary of agreed items and next steps:

Agreed items:
- Term: we will proceed with a 24-month term per customer request (option A) with the adjusted year-1 unit price as discussed; Marcus will include a side-by-side price table in the execution form.
- Termination for convenience: 45-day notice; pro-rated refund for unused committed capacity calculated as (unused days remaining / total days in term) * prepaid committed units. Language included in attached order form.
- Data residency & SOC2: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and a current subprocessor list prior to signature.
- Timeline: target to have signed order form and PO by Dec 10; provisioning to begin Jan 1, 2028.

Next steps:
1) Attached is the execution-ready order form (OrderForm_v4_for_signature.docx) with Laura’s legal language and the pricing table.
2) Elaine: please confirm PO number and we will send DocuSign for signature.
